problem_statement: The Mazouni Magazine imagePaths texture WebGL renderer public/512 AeonikTRIAL-Regular Vite TypeScript project is a runnable Three.js portfolio surface with a full-screen canvas, a local Aeonik font, thirteen poster images under public/512, a texture-atlas implementation in src/magazine.ts, and wheel plus touch browsing after the intro animation. The translucent Atlas Flow overlay that floats over the poster stack should become an interactive frame browser: a rail of the thirteen poster frames (p1 to p13) plus an Advance frame control and a live readout that names the current frame as Frame N of 13 · 512/pN.jpg. The overlay must stay complete and legible across desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile without horizontal overflow, and must not replace the canvas, shaders, texture atlas, wheel handling, touch handling, or original portfolio identity.
required_content: Turn the Atlas Flow overlay into an interactive frame browser: a rail of the thirteen poster frames plus an Advance frame control and a live readout.
The live readout must name the current frame using the real local poster path, e.g. Frame 1 of 13 · 512/p1.jpg, and advance through the p1-to-p13 sequence when the control is used.
The overlay must explicitly reference the real local poster asset sequence, including 512/p1.jpg to 512/p13.jpg or equivalent p1-to-p13 public/512 path cues.
Name the Texture Atlas, Poster Sequence, Thirteen Frames, Wheel Browse, Touch Drag, and Aeonik Editorial concepts tied to the existing implementation.
The full overlay (frame rail, control, and readout) must render on desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile alike, and the frame rail must not cause horizontal overflow on any viewport.
Keep Chakib Mazouni, Web Developer & Designer, Freelance, 2022-2025, 10 rue de la Paix, 75002 Paris France, X/Twitter, LinkedIn, Github, 2025, W21, and M30 visible in captured states.

Implement the change in source used by the Vite build; do not edit only generated dist output or hide completion text in comments, metadata, ARIA-only labels, CSS class names, script strings, image alt text, or console output.

Preserve the Three.js Magazine class, canvas#webgl renderer, shader pipeline, local public/512 images, Aeonik font assets, wheel listener, touch listener, and responsive full-viewport canvas behavior.
design_constraints: Preserve the dark editorial WebGL mood, sparse Aeonik typography, amber-white text color, fixed full-viewport canvas, and poster-stack composition as the primary visual identity.
The frame rail and its chips must wrap and stay legible; chips must not overgrow, overlap, or collapse into an illegible dark-on-dark pile that buries the overlay or canvas.
The Advance frame control must genuinely update the readout to the current frame; a click that toggles the active chip but leaves the readout frozen is incorrect.
Use existing local poster and font assets as the content source; do not introduce remote stock images, generated media, unrelated icons, or dummy gallery copy.
Desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile layouts must avoid horizontal overflow and keep labels such as 512/p1.jpg to 512/p13.jpg, Texture Atlas, and Poster Sequence readable.
Do not remove or bypass src/magazine.ts, src/canvas.ts, src/shaders, public/512, public/Aeonik TRIAL, or the normal npm/Vite build path.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial, and mobile_initial must retain the original portfolio chrome, a nonblank WebGL surface, and the restyled flow layer without layout overflow.
desktop_after_intro must show the page after the intro timeline while retaining the flow layer and canvas poster-stack context.
desktop_wheel_forward and desktop_wheel_reverse must remain action-clean states after dispatched wheel events, proving the overlay does not block or replace browsing behavior.
desktop_pointer_right must remain action-clean after a pointer movement state over the canvas.
mobile_after_intro must keep the flow text readable at 390px while preserving the original footer markers and canvas layout.

change_completion: A visible editorial flow layer is added to the existing WebGL magazine page with the required asset-flow and interaction labels.
The layer references the real p1-to-p13 local poster texture sequence and existing wheel/touch browsing behavior rather than generic gallery copy.
The implementation edits source consumed by the Vite build and does not rely on generated dist output.
design_consistency: The full-screen dark canvas and sparse portfolio chrome remain dominant, with the new layer integrated as restrained editorial metadata.
Typography, color, spacing, and surface treatment stay consistent with the Aeonik magazine/portfolio style.
Desktop, tablet, mobile, wheel, pointer, and after-intro states avoid horizontal overflow and text collisions.
regression: Original portfolio identity, contact links, footer markers, canvas rendering, texture-atlas loading, wheel navigation, and touch navigation remain intact.
The implementation does not replace the WebGL magazine with static screenshots, DOM-only thumbnails, or a detached route.
The Vite TypeScript build continues to complete through the existing package scripts.
responsive: The added flow layer remains readable in desktop, tablet, mobile initial, and mobile after-intro states.
Long asset path labels wrap within the overlay at 390px without hiding footer markers or forcing document overflow.
Interactive wheel and pointer states retain stable layout after actions.

author_notes: Slot 149 is an L2 content/asset-continuity restyle task. It targets the missing user-facing explanation of a real local WebGL texture atlas, not a functional rewrite. The state plan protects the existing portfolio chrome, nonblank canvas captures, wheel/pointer interaction states, and mobile readability while the submission verifier checks that completion cues are rendered as visible page text.
